In the given congruence, we have $a=10$ and $n=45$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(10,45)=5.
$$

Since $b=35$ is divisible by $5,$ our congruence has $5$ solutions.

First, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}10x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ 5\cdot 2x & ≡5\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,5\cdot 9) \\ \cancel{5}\cdot 2x & ≡\cancel{5}\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{5}\cdot 9) \\ 2x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=2$ and ${n}_{1}=9$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(2,9)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $9.$

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $2\,(\text{mod}\,9).$ To find the inverse of $2\,(\text{mod}\,9),$ we compute the exponents of $2\,(\text{mod}\,9)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,9):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {2}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 2≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {2}^{4} & ≡8\cdot 2≡16≡9+7≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {2}^{5} & ≡7\cdot 2≡14≡9+5≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {2}^{6} & ≡5\cdot 2≡10≡9+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $5\cdot 2≡1\,(\text{mod}\,9),$ which means that $5$ is the multiplicative inverse of $2$ (modulo $9$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ 5\cdot 2x & ≡5\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ (5\cdot 2)x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ x & ≡3\cdot 9+8 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ x & ≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡8\,(\text{mod}\,9).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $45$ (not modulo $9$). To find all the solutions modulo $45,$ we repeatedly add $9$ modulo $45$ until we reach the number $8$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡8+9≡17 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡17+9≡26 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡26+9≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡35+9≡44 &  & (\text{mod}\,45) \\ {x}_{6} & ≡44+9≡53≡45+8≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,45)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3,4,5}≡8,\,17,\,26,\,35,\,44\,(\text{mod}\,45).
$$
